title: Restore complete newest-version activity evidence in optimization ranking
description:
As an optimization operator, I want portfolio ranking to distinguish a valid champion/version history from a dangling champion identifier, so that structurally ineligible scores do not incorrectly make otherwise complete activity coverage fail.

Observed platform defect: the exhaustive score inventory can return a scalar champion version identifier while both the champion relationship and reverse version history are empty. Ranking currently treats that row as otherwise eligible and reports missing activity evidence. The fix must use the existing exhaustive GraphQL query, preserve opaque identifiers, include unpromoted versions for valid scores, and add no per-score reads.

Feature: Correctly classify inaccessible score versions

Scenario: A score has a dangling champion identifier
Given an exhaustive score inventory row has a champion version identifier
And its champion version relationship is null
And its reverse version history is empty
When optimization ranking evaluates eligibility
Then it classifies the score as structurally unranked with an explicit invalid-champion reason
And it does not classify the row as incomplete cooldown activity evidence
And the structurally ineligible row does not make otherwise complete portfolio activity coverage incomplete

Scenario: A valid score has a newer unpromoted version
Given the champion relationship is valid
And the reverse version history contains a newer unpromoted version
When optimization ranking evaluates cooldown activity
Then it uses the newest version timestamp rather than the champion timestamp
And preserves the newest version opaque identifier unchanged

Scenario: An otherwise eligible score still lacks newest-version evidence
Given the champion relationship is valid
And newest-version activity cannot be established
When optimization ranking runs
Then the score fails closed
And the portfolio is not exact
And the primary next action reports evidence repair rather than rank completion

Out of scope: data repair, score mutation, optimizer launch, and cooldown-policy changes.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Production-shaped read-only dogfood evidence reproduced the defect safely: exhaustive scorecard enumeration completed, while a subset of versioned scores returned no reverse newest-version row. Implementation will begin with failing outside-in specifications and will not weaken cooldown semantics or add per-score reads.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: A direct production GraphQL check showed an affected scalar champion identifier resolves to null and the indexed version list for that score is empty. The implementation plan is simplified: expose the champion relationship in the existing exhaustive inventory, classify dangling pointers as structural ineligibility, and retain newest-version cooldown checks for valid scores.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented the minimal GraphQL-path fix: exhaustive inventory now resolves the champion relationship, dangling scalar pointers are structurally unranked, valid scores still use newest version history for cooldown, and incomplete packets request coverage repair. The focused optimization/runtime suite passes 340 tests, and a read-only integration verification now returns exact activity coverage with no activity-evidence failures. The issue remains open until merge.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Terminology correction: the observable condition is an unresolved champion reference, not proof that a champion configuration is invalid. The public unranked reason and documentation will use unresolved_champion_reference before the next dogfood run.
